figures.title: Composition and within-type RNA contributions
figures.caption: Age-associated RNA differences combine captured composition and within-type changes. Cdkn2a detection rises in lung and falls in bladder. Values are 24 minus 3 months, with equal mouse weighting on common cell types. Four terms sum to the total; they are descriptive accounting, not causal effects. Color scales differ between panels.

figures.title: Within-type profiles and fixed-composition animal estimates
figures.caption: Within-type profiles locate age-associated RNA differences; fixed young composition asks whether population redistribution accounts for the tissue summary. A/B: 24 minus 3 months. C/D: connected values from each mouse; black bars, means; triangles, females. Sparse types and finer subtype mixtures remain unresolved. RNA detection does not establish senescence.

figures.title: Tissue-local T-cell clonality across ages
figures.caption: Local T-cell clone repetition is higher in older thymus and spleen samples; marrow shows a different age pattern. Points are mice and black bars are means. Bottom panels condition on tissue-specific sampling depth, so their magnitudes are not directly comparable across tissues. T-cell subtype, assembly selection and function remain unresolved.

figures.title: Compartment representation and cross-tissue clone sharing
figures.caption: Older local-clone burden persists after fixing tissue representation in the same mice. A–C use mice with thymus, spleen and marrow; D uses all supported mice per tissue. Shared clones indicate observed distribution across tissues, not migration. Only two young mice support the balanced comparison; subtype and reconstruction selection remain alternatives.

limits: Exposed exploratory observations; all panels use frozen outputs, no new model or biological acceptance.
